correctness.rationale: In K4 square Kn, a blocked shortest path exists exactly for a fully selected 2-by-2 rectangle. Pair-consumption over six edges of K4 partitions every admissible selected set into size-two-only, one triple, or one quadruple. Each contribution is directly counted with injective falling factorial assignments. A maximal set cannot contain an empty column; singleton rows must be degree-three in the consumed-pair graph and all doubled columns must satisfy the edge-covering criterion. A connected four-vertex graph satisfying this criterion is exactly K1,3, C4, K4-e, or K4; n>=6 excludes C4 since it has no permitted singleton rows. Exact family counts yield the claimed four polynomial coefficients, and a ratio expansion gives the stated asymptotic. An independent brute-force/geodesic checker reproduces all 1,587,227 admissible sets across widths 2 to 6 and tests all one-vertex extensions. Finite experiments are not used as a substitute for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The four-row rook graph is a canonical nontrivial Cartesian product, and the entire mutually visible placement distribution and terminal spectrum are natural graph invariants. The four strict maximal cardinalities extend the previously known lower endpoint to a complete and quantitatively heterogeneous spectrum. Exact multiplicities show that nearly every uniformly chosen terminal placement is maximum-size, unlike the existence of many smaller maximal configurations. The row-pair classification is structural and supports reproducible counts for all widths, not an arbitrary finite data lookup.
